name: Ocellaris Clownfish
notes: Hardy and iconic. Pairs easily with another clown; can host anemones.

name: Percula Clownfish
notes: True Percula clownfish with prominent black outlines. Peaceful reef inhabitant.

name: Blue Green Chromis
notes: Active schooling damselfish. Shimmers bright metallic aqua. Keep in odd-numbered groups.

name: Yellow Tang
notes: Classic reef centerpiece. Voracious grazer on filamentous algae.

name: Blue / Hippo Tang
notes: Active swimmer, needs ample horizontal swimming space. Prone to ich if stressed.

name: Royal Gramma
notes: Stunning violet-and-yellow coloration. Caves and rock crevices are essential.

name: Firefish Goby
notes: Peaceful dartfish with high dorsal fin. Known jumper—requires a tight tank lid.

name: Yellow Watchman Goby
notes: Bottom dweller with charismatic grumpy face. Forms a famous symbiotic bond with pistol shrimp.

name: Diamond Watchman Goby
notes: Master sand-sifter. Continuously filters sand bed through gills, keeping sand spotless.

name: Lawnmower Blenny
notes: Excellent natural grazer for nuisance hair algae and microalgae films.

name: Tailspot Blenny
notes: Small, comical nano fish. Perches on rocks and pecks at microalgae.

name: Six Line Wrasse
notes: Active hunter that eats nuisance flatworms, bristleworms, and pyramid snails.

name: Banggai Cardinalfish
notes: Gentle, slow-moving fish with striking black and silver stripes. Mouthbrooder.

name: Clarkii Clownfish
notes: Hardy and bold. Hosts nearly every clown-hosting anemone. Can get pushy as it matures.

name: Maroon Clownfish
notes: Largest and most aggressive clown. Females get big. Best added last and kept with robust tankmates.

name: Tomato Clownfish
notes: Very hardy but territorial. Often pairs with a bubble tip anemone.

name: Pink Skunk Clownfish
notes: Small and more timid than most clowns. Keep away from aggressive tankmates.

name: Cinnamon Clownfish
notes: Hardy with a dark body and white head bar. Territorial once paired.

name: Black Axil Chromis
notes: Looks like a green chromis with a dark spot at the pectoral fin base. Groups can thin out through bickering.

name: Lyretail Anthias
notes: Colorful shoaling fish. Feed two or more times daily. Keep one male with several females.

name: Bartlett's Anthias
notes: One of the more peaceful anthias. Needs frequent feeding and open swimming room.

name: Sunburst Anthias
notes: Shy cave-dweller that often swims upside down under ledges. Prefers dimmer spots.

name: Pajama Cardinalfish
notes: Peaceful and slow. Most active at dusk. Very easy to feed.

name: Threadfin Cardinalfish
notes: Small peaceful shoaling cardinal. May be eaten by large or aggressive fish.

name: Yellowtail Blue Damselfish
notes: Among the milder damsels. Bright blue with a yellow tail. Territorial around rockwork.

name: Azure Damselfish
notes: Hardy with blue and yellow split coloration. Can harass new additions.

name: Starck's Damselfish
notes: Striking electric blue and yellow. Less commonly available and fairly territorial.

name: Domino Damselfish
notes: Extremely hardy but very aggressive as an adult. Think twice before adding to a peaceful reef.

name: Three-Stripe Damselfish
notes: Tough and territorial with bold black and white bars. Hard to remove once settled.

name: Purple Tang
notes: Deep purple with a yellow tail. Can be aggressive toward other tangs. Needs a large tank.

name: Scopas Tang
notes: Hardy grazer similar in shape to a yellow tang. Needs swimming room and can bully similar fish.

name: Sailfin Tang
notes: Grows large with tall fins. Needs a long tank as an adult.

name: Kole Tang
notes: Bristle-tooth grazer that combs rock and glass for film algae. Generally one of the calmer tangs.

name: Tomini Tang
notes: One of the smaller tangs. Good film algae grazer and fairly peaceful.

name: Powder Blue Tang
notes: Beautiful but ich-prone and aggressive toward other tangs. Quarantine carefully. Needs a large tank.

name: Powder Brown Tang
notes: Often a little hardier than the powder blue. Still ich-prone and needs plenty of swimming room.

name: Achilles Tang
notes: Needs very high flow and oxygen plus a big tank. Very ich-prone. Not for beginners.

name: Naso Tang
notes: Grows large and needs a long tank. Loves brown seaweed.

name: Foxface Rabbitfish
notes: Hardy and peaceful grazer but may nip some corals. Venomous fin spines: handle with care.

name: Magnificent Foxface
notes: Close relative of the foxface with bolder markings. Venomous fin spines.

name: Flame Angelfish
notes: Vivid orange-red dwarf angel. May nip clams and fleshy corals.

name: Coral Beauty Angelfish
notes: Among the hardier dwarf angels. May nip LPS and clam mantles.

name: Lemonpeel Angelfish
notes: Bright yellow dwarf angel. Known for nipping corals more than some others.

name: Cherub Angelfish
notes: Tiny Atlantic dwarf angel. Hardy and suitable for smaller tanks.

name: Potter's Angelfish
notes: Hawaiian dwarf angel. Often harder to acclimate. Needs a mature tank with plenty of grazing.

name: Bellus Angelfish
notes: Swallowtail angel that feeds in open water. Generally leaves corals alone.

name: Watanabei Angelfish
notes: Reef-friendly swallowtail angel. Needs swimming room and frequent feeding.

name: Emperor Angelfish
notes: Spectacular color change into adulthood. Needs a very large tank. Often nips corals and clams.

name: Queen Angelfish
notes: Large Atlantic angel that grazes on sponges and corals. Best in a big fish-only system.

name: Melanurus Wrasse
notes: Hunts pests such as pyramid snails. May eat small shrimp and snails. Needs a sand bed to sleep in.

name: Yellow Coris Wrasse
notes: Bright yellow and hardy. Buries in sand at night. Sometimes helps with flatworms.

name: Christmas Wrasse
notes: Red and green ornate wrasse. Needs sand. May eat small inverts.

name: McCosker's Flasher Wrasse
notes: Males flash brilliant colors when displaying. Needs a tight lid because it jumps.

name: Carpenter's Flasher Wrasse
notes: Peaceful flasher wrasse. Keep one male with several females. Known jumper.

name: Solar Fairy Wrasse
notes: Colorful and active reef wrasse. Sleeps in a mucus cocoon. Needs a tight lid.

name: Lubbock's Fairy Wrasse
notes: Smaller fairy wrasse that fits mid-sized reefs well. Known jumper.

name: Exquisite Fairy Wrasse
notes: Active swimmer with shimmering color. Needs a tight lid.

name: Possum Wrasse
notes: Tiny secretive wrasse that hides in rock. Needs small meaty foods.

name: Mystery Wrasse
notes: Colorful relative of the six line. Can be territorial toward similar wrasses.

name: Leopard Wrasse
notes: Beautiful but often hard to get feeding. Best in a mature tank full of pods with a sand bed.

name: Bluestreak Cleaner Wrasse
notes: Specialized cleaner that often starves in captivity. Generally best left in the ocean.

name: Dragon Wrasse
notes: Flips rocks and rearranges the tank. Eats inverts and small fish. Best in a fish-only system.

name: Harlequin Tuskfish
notes: Striking banded fish with blue teeth. Eats crustaceans. Needs a large tank.

name: Yellow Clown Goby
notes: Tiny fish that perches among coral branches. May nip SPS polyps. Good for nano tanks.

name: Green Clown Goby
notes: Small coral-perching goby with red lines. May nip SPS polyps.

name: Neon Goby
notes: Small cleaner goby. Captive-bred fish are widely available and hardy.

name: Purple Firefish
notes: Peaceful dartfish with purple fins. Known jumper. Needs a tight lid.

name: Bluecheek Goby
notes: Constantly sifts sand. Needs a mature deep sand bed to find enough food. Known jumper.

name: Randall's Shrimp Goby
notes: Pairs with pistol shrimp. Stands guard at the burrow entrance. Needs sand.

name: Yasha Goby
notes: Small striped goby with a tall dorsal fin. Pairs with Randall's pistol shrimp.

name: Court Jester Goby
notes: Needs a mature tank with plenty of natural food to pick at. Often thins out in new tanks.

name: Scissortail Dartfish
notes: Peaceful open-water swimmer. Bolts when startled and jumps: use a tight lid.

name: Zebra Dartfish
notes: Peaceful with fine vertical bars. Can be kept in small groups in larger tanks. Known jumper.

name: Engineer Goby
notes: Not a true goby. Digs extensive tunnels under rock so build rockwork on the glass. Long-lived.

name: Midas Blenny
notes: Golden fish that swims in the open and perches on rock with lots of personality.

name: Bicolor Blenny
notes: Hardy algae picker with two-tone coloring. May nip at larger polyps on occasion.

name: Starry Blenny
notes: Algae grazer dotted with white spots. Needs a mature tank with plenty of algae growth.

name: Canary Fang Blenny
notes: Bright yellow open-water blenny. Has venomous fangs but is peaceful and rarely a problem.

name: Black Combtooth Blenny
notes: Larger combtooth blenny. Grazes film algae and perches on rocks.

name: Orchid Dottyback
notes: Vivid magenta and among the most peaceful dottybacks. Captive-bred fish are common.

name: Neon Dottyback
notes: Hardy orange and neon-blue fish. Often aggressive: pick tankmates carefully.

name: Sunrise Dottyback
notes: Blue and yellow with moderate aggression. May harass small shrimp.

name: Black Cap Basslet
notes: Purple body with a black cap. Hardy cave-dweller. Territorial toward its own kind.

name: Swissguard Basslet
notes: Shy striped fish that stays in caves. May eat tiny shrimp.

name: Chalk Bass
notes: Small hardy Atlantic bass. Unusually peaceful and can be kept in groups.

name: Harlequin Bass
notes: Handsome black and white bass. Will eat small shrimp and small fish.

name: Yellow Assessor
notes: Peaceful cave-dweller that often swims upside down under overhangs.

name: Blue Assessor
notes: Deep blue relative of the yellow assessor. Shy at first and peaceful.

name: Green Mandarin Dragonet
notes: Often starves in young tanks. Needs a mature pod population or a fish trained to frozen food.

name: Spotted Mandarin Dragonet
notes: Same pod-hungry needs as the green mandarin. Add only to mature tanks.

name: Scooter Dragonet
notes: Often sold as a scooter blenny but it is a dragonet. Needs pods. Males fight.

name: Ruby Red Dragonet
notes: Tiny red dragonet. Needs a good pod supply. Males fight.

name: Flame Hawkfish
notes: Perches on coral heads and watches everything. May eat small shrimp.

name: Longnose Hawkfish
notes: Checkered fish with a long snout. May eat small shrimp. Known jumper.

name: Arc-Eye Hawkfish
notes: Hardy perching predator. Will hunt shrimp and small crabs.

name: Copperband Butterflyfish
notes: Famous for sometimes eating aiptasia. Can be hard to feed. Needs a mature tank.

name: Raccoon Butterflyfish
notes: Hardy butterfly that eats aiptasia but also corals and inverts. Best kept outside a reef.

name: Pearlscale Butterflyfish
notes: Attractive and comparatively hardy butterfly. May nip corals.

name: Longnose Butterflyfish
notes: Bright yellow with a long snout that can pick at tube worms and polyps.

name: Lined Seahorse
notes: Best in a dedicated low-flow tank. Avoid stinging corals and fast feeders.

name: Bluestripe Pipefish
notes: Thin and delicate. Needs small live or frozen foods and calm tankmates.

name: Snowflake Moray Eel
notes: Hardy eel that hunts crustaceans at night. Secure lid required because eels escape.

name: Dwarf Fuzzy Lionfish
notes: Small lionfish. Venomous spines. Eats small fish and shrimp.

name: Fu Manchu Lionfish
notes: Shy nocturnal dwarf lion. Often hard to feed. Venomous spines.

name: Volitans Lionfish
notes: Large predator that eats anything it can swallow. Venomous spines. Needs a very large tank.

name: Picasso Triggerfish
notes: Hardy with wild markings. Will eat inverts and rearrange rocks. Best in a fish-only tank.

name: Niger Triggerfish
notes: One of the calmer triggers. May still eat shrimp and crabs. Needs a big tank.

name: Bluejaw Triggerfish
notes: Open-water planktivore that is friendlier to reefs than most triggers. Watch small inverts.

name: Valentini Puffer
notes: Small sharpnose puffer. May nip corals and inverts. Toxic if eaten by a tankmate.

name: Porcupine Puffer
notes: Engaging personality but messy. Needs shelled foods to wear down its beak. Eats inverts.

name: Longhorn Cowfish
notes: Can release toxin when stressed or dying and wipe out a tank. Grows large.

name: Matted Filefish
notes: Often bought to eat aiptasia. Results vary and it may nip soft corals and zoanthids.

name: Trochus Snail
notes: Top-tier algae snail. Can upright itself if flipped upside down.

name: Nassarius Snail
notes: Burrows under the sand bed, emerges like a zombie when fish are fed to clean leftover food.

name: Astraea Snail
notes: Classic glass and live-rock grazer with pyramid shell. Cannot flip itself if overturned.

name: Cerith Snail
notes: Cleans glass, rock crevices, and burrows into sand bed eating detritus and diatoms.

name: Mexican Turbo Snail
notes: Bulldozer snail that demolishes thick green hair algae.

name: Blue Leg Hermit Crab
notes: Miniature scavenger. Scours rock holes for detritus and nuisance algae. Provide empty shells.

name: Scarlet Reef Hermit Crab
notes: The most peaceful hermit crab. Bright red legs with yellow eye stalks.

name: Emerald Crab
notes: Famous for controlling nuisance Valonia (bubble algae).

name: Peppermint Shrimp
notes: Popular aiptasia eater but results vary. Several look-alike species are sold under this name.

name: Sand-Sifting Starfish
notes: Strips sand beds of life and then starves. Needs a very large mature sand bed.

name: Fighting Conch
notes: Great sand bed grazer that keeps sand turned over. Does not actually fight.

name: Queen Conch
notes: Grows large. Excellent sand grazer for bigger systems with mature sand.

name: Margarita Snail
notes: Cool-water snail that often lives only briefly in warm reef tanks.

name: Nerite Snail
notes: Good on glass and rock. Tends to climb out above the water line so use a lid.

name: Stomatella Snail
notes: Fast flat-bodied grazer that often appears on its own and breeds readily in reefs.

name: Bumblebee Snail
notes: Small striped scavenger. May prey on other small snails and worms.

name: Money Cowrie
notes: Small algae-grazing cowrie with a smooth glossy shell.

name: Tiger Cowrie
notes: Large and beautiful. Can bulldoze corals and may eat sponges and soft corals.

name: Abalone
notes: Excellent rock and glass grazer. Sensitive to low oxygen. Do not pry it off rock.

name: Dwarf Zebra Hermit Crab
notes: Hardy little scavenger. May attack snails for their shells. Provide spares.

name: Electric Blue Hermit Crab
notes: Brilliant blue legs. May attack snails for their shells. Provide spares.

name: Halloween Hermit Crab
notes: Orange and red banded legs. Larger and sometimes bothers snails and small inverts.

name: Sally Lightfoot Crab
notes: Fast flat crab that grazes hair algae. Larger ones may become opportunistic.

name: Tiger Tail Sea Cucumber
notes: Cleans sand and hides by day. Can release toxin if injured. Guard pump intakes.

name: Pink and Black Sea Cucumber
notes: Pink underside and dark top. Good sand cleaner. Can release toxin if injured.

name: Micro Brittle Star
notes: Tiny scavenger that often appears on its own. A harmless sign of a healthy tank.

name: Red Serpent Star
notes: Smooth-armed nighttime scavenger. Generally safer than green brittle stars.

name: Green Brittle Star
notes: Large and able to catch small sleeping fish and shrimp. Think carefully before adding.

name: Pincushion Urchin
notes: Strong algae grazer. Can knock over loose coral frags and rockwork.

name: Longspine Urchin
notes: Powerful algae grazer with sharp venomous spines. Needs a big tank.

name: Pencil Urchin
notes: Thick blunt spines. May graze on corals and encrusting life.

name: Copepods
notes: Tiny live food that also cleans. Seed these before adding mandarins and other pod eaters.

name: Amphipods
notes: Tiny crustaceans that hide in rock and clean. A valuable natural food source for fish.

name: Skunk Cleaner Shrimp
notes: Bold and friendly. Sets up cleaning stations where fish queue to have parasites removed.

name: Blood Red Fire Shrimp
notes: Deep crimson red with striking white antennae and legs. Shy scavenger.

name: Tiger Pistol Shrimp
notes: Excavates elaborate underground burrows shared with watchman gobies.

name: Bubble Tip Anemone (BTA)
notes: Natural host for clownfish. Requires stable mature water parameters and good lighting.

name: Tuxedo Urchin
notes: Voracious algae grazer that covers itself with small debris and shells for camouflage.

name: Harlequin Shrimp
notes: Stunning but eats only live starfish. Plan a long-term food supply before buying.

name: Sexy Shrimp
notes: Tiny dancing shrimp ideal for nanos. May nibble zoanthids and anemones.

name: Coral Banded Shrimp
notes: Hardy and showy. Aggressive toward other shrimp and may grab small fish.

name: Camel Shrimp
notes: Hardy and striped but often nips soft corals and polyps. Best in groups.

name: Randall's Pistol Shrimp
notes: Small red and white pistol shrimp. Classic partner for yasha and other shrimp gobies.

name: Pederson Cleaner Shrimp
notes: Small transparent cleaner that lives among anemones. Watch out for large predators.

name: Bumblebee Shrimp
notes: Tiny striped shrimp for quiet nano tanks. Easily eaten by larger fish.

name: Pom Pom Crab
notes: Tiny boxer crab that holds small anemones in its claws like pom poms. Easily lost in rockwork.

name: Porcelain Crab
notes: Filter-feeding crab that lives in anemones. Feed fine foods.

name: Arrow Crab
notes: Spindly long-legged crab that can catch bristleworms but may harass shrimp.

name: Decorator Crab
notes: Covers itself in sponge and algae. Fun to watch but may snip corals to wear them.

name: Red Reef Lobster
notes: Small reef lobster that is active at night. Can prey on small fish and shrimp.

name: Peacock Mantis Shrimp
notes: Spectacular but needs its own tank. Its strike is strong enough to crack thin glass.

name: Feather Duster Worm
notes: Fan-shaped tube worm. Needs fine foods. May be nipped by angels and butterflies.

name: Christmas Tree Worm
notes: Colorful spirals living in rock or coral. Often sold on a live coral head.

name: Flame Scallop
notes: Eye-catching but often starves. Needs frequent fine feeding and a mature tank.

name: Maxima Clam
notes: Vivid mantle. Needs strong light and stable alkalinity. Sensitive when small.

name: Crocea Clam
notes: Small burrowing clam with an intense mantle. Needs very strong light. Place on rock.

name: Derasa Clam
notes: Among the hardiest giant clams. Tolerates moderate light. Place on sand or rubble.

name: Squamosa Clam
notes: Fluted shell with a patterned mantle. Moderate to high light. Place on sand or rubble.

name: Blue Linckia Starfish
notes: Striking but ships poorly. Needs slow careful acclimation and a very mature tank.

name: Chocolate Chip Starfish
notes: Hardy but eats corals and clams along with other sessile inverts. Not for reef tanks.

name: Sea Hare
notes: Big appetite for hair algae. Often starves once the algae is gone. Guard pump intakes.

name: Berghia Nudibranch
notes: The namesake sea slug. Eats only aiptasia and starves once it runs out. Guard intakes and avoid predators.

name: Lettuce Sea Slug
notes: Often sold as a lettuce nudibranch but is a sacoglossan. Feeds on algae and needs a steady supply.

name: Green Star Polyps (GSP)
notes: Extremely hardy neon green mat. Keep on an isolated rock island to prevent spreading over rockwork.

name: Zoanthids & Palys
notes: Vibrant button polyps in endless color morphs. Note: Handle with care due to palytoxin.

name: Duncan Coral
notes: Hardy LPS coral with large green fleshy polyps. Spawns new heads rapidly.

name: Hammer Coral
notes: Waving tentacles with hammer-shaped tips. Moderate light and gentle oscillating flow.

name: Torch Coral
notes: Prized long waving tentacles with glowing tips. Keep space between it and other non-Euphyllia.

name: Frogspawn Coral
notes: Multilobed tentacles resembling frog eggs. Hardy and stunning under blue actinics.

name: Candy Cane Coral
notes: Hardy trumpet-shaped LPS coral. Extends feeder tentacles at night.

name: Montipora Cap
notes: The best beginner SPS coral. Forms stunning swirling plates under good lighting.

name: Toadstool Leather Coral
notes: Hardy mushroom-shaped soft coral with long flowing polyp tentacles.

name: Pulsing Xenia
notes: Pulsing soft coral that can spread fast. Isolate it on its own rock.

name: Kenya Tree Coral
notes: Very hardy tree-shaped soft coral. Drops branches and spreads readily.

name: Finger Leather Coral
notes: Hardy soft coral. Can release chemicals that affect SPS so run carbon.

name: Cabbage Leather Coral
notes: Flat ruffled leather coral that does well in low to moderate light.

name: Devil's Hand Leather Coral
notes: Tough finger-lobed leather coral. Sheds a waxy layer from time to time.

name: Colt Coral
notes: Soft bushy coral that sways in flow. Grows fast and may need trimming.

name: Clove Polyps
notes: Fast-spreading mat coral with feathery polyps. Isolate it on its own rock.

name: Anthelia
notes: Waving hand soft coral. Can spread rapidly across rockwork.

name: Yellow Polyps
notes: Hardy golden polyps that spread slowly. Handle with gloves like other zoanthid relatives.

name: Pipe Organ Coral
notes: Red skeleton with green polyps. Appreciates moderate flow and stable water.

name: Discosoma Mushroom
notes: Hardy low-light mushroom. Can overgrow and sting neighbors over time.

name: Rhodactis Mushroom
notes: Hairy-looking mushroom that handles low light and low flow. Give it some space.

name: Bounce Mushroom
notes: Prized bubble-covered mushroom. Expensive and slower to settle than most mushrooms.

name: Ricordea Florida
notes: Bubbly Atlantic mushroom in many colors. Loves a mature tank and small meaty foods.

name: Ricordea Yuma
notes: Pacific ricordea with a multicolored center. Needs moderate light and low to moderate flow.

name: Sea Rod Gorgonian
notes: Photosynthetic Caribbean gorgonian. Needs good flow to shed its waxy coating.

name: Sea Fan
notes: Fan-shaped gorgonian. Place it across steady flow.

name: Carnation Coral
notes: Non-photosynthetic and hard to keep alive. Needs constant very fine feeding.

name: Sun Coral
notes: Non-photosynthetic orange polyps. Needs individual target feeding. Thrives under overhangs.

name: Goniopora
notes: Flowerpot coral with long polyps. Has improved in captivity but is still often short-lived.

name: Alveopora
notes: Similar to goniopora with twelve tentacles per polyp. Needs mature stable water.

name: Bubble Coral
notes: Inflated bubble tissue by day and long stinging sweepers at night. Give it plenty of room.

name: Open Brain Coral
notes: Sits on sand with low flow. Large fleshy polyp that loves to be fed.

name: Lobophyllia
notes: Colorful fleshy LPS. Needs lower flow and space because it sends out sweepers at night.

name: Acan Lord
notes: Colorful LPS often sold as Acanthastrea. Low to moderate light. Feeds eagerly at night.

name: Acan Echinata
notes: Fleshy encrusting LPS. Does well on rock and can be aggressive to close neighbors.

name: Blastomussa
notes: Hardy low-light LPS with round polyps. Fairly peaceful and good in shaded spots.

name: Favia
notes: Moon coral often still sold as Favia. Extends sweeper tentacles at night.

name: Favites
notes: Honeycomb brain coral with shared polyp walls. Gives off sweepers at night.

name: Chalice Coral
notes: Plating LPS with vivid colored mouths. Moderate light and flow. Can sting neighbors.

name: Plate Coral
notes: Free-living coral for the sand bed. Can inflate and move. Keep clear of neighbors.

name: Elegance Coral
notes: Stunning but delicate and very aggressive. Place on sand in low to moderate flow.

name: Galaxea
notes: Fine tubular LPS with very long powerful sweepers. Give it a wide buffer zone.

name: Scroll Coral
notes: Plating coral that does best with good light and moderate flow. Often quite durable.

name: Branching Hammer Coral
notes: Branching form of hammer coral. Moderate light and flow. Sweepers need space.

name: Scolymia
notes: Round single-polyp LPS. Low light and low flow. Feed regularly.

name: Button Coral
notes: Translucent inflated single-polyp LPS. Likes the sand bed in low flow.

name: Birdsnest Coral
notes: Fine-branching SPS with strong light and flow. Often the first branching SPS a keeper tries.

name: Stylophora
notes: Fast-growing branching SPS. Good light and flow. Comes in pink and green.

name: Pocillopora
notes: Fast-growing and forgiving SPS. Can spread on its own through tiny larvae.

name: Montipora Digitata
notes: Finger-like and fast-growing. Among the easier SPS to start with.

name: Montipora Setosa
notes: Short fine branching SPS popular for bright colors. Needs strong light and flow.

name: Acropora Millepora
notes: Classic staghorn-style SPS. Needs very stable alkalinity with strong light and flow.

name: Acropora Tenuis
notes: Fast-growing table-forming SPS. Needs very stable water plus strong light and flow.

name: Psammocora
notes: Encrusting SPS with a velvety texture. Moderate light and flow.

name: Hydnophora
notes: Horn coral that grows branches. Its sweepers sting neighbors despite small polyps.

name: Leptoseris
notes: Thin plating coral that tolerates lower light well. Vulnerable to being shaded or stung.

name: Porites
notes: Slow-growing stony coral. Durable once settled. Watch for red bugs and flatworms.

name: Cyphastrea
notes: Encrusting stony coral. Tolerant of low to moderate light and a good first small-polyp coral.

name: Pavona Cactus Coral
notes: Thin upright plates. Moderate light and flow. Can spread over time.

name: Rock Flower Anemone
notes: Colorful Atlantic anemone that tends to stay put. Usually does not host clownfish.

name: Long Tentacle Anemone
notes: Buries its foot in sand and hosts clownfish. Guard pump intakes because anemones can wander.

name: Mini Maxi Carpet Anemone
notes: Small colorful carpet anemone. Strong sting and can wander. Guard pump intakes.

name: Condylactis Anemone
notes: Atlantic anemone with purple-tipped tentacles. Rarely hosts clownfish. Can sting neighbors.

name: Sebae Anemone
notes: Long-tentacled host anemone. Often bleached when sold. Avoid white specimens.

name: Ritteri Anemone
notes: Spectacular but demanding. Needs intense light and strong flow. Likes high perches.

name: Haddon's Carpet Anemone
notes: Very large with a powerful sting that can catch fish. Needs a big mature tank.
